_comment: Classes, levels 1-10. Features are simplified 5e (SRD 5.1, CC-BY-4.0), fought on the battle grid. 'rule' tags are used by game systems; kits are starting equipment packages (item ids from items.json).

fighter.name: Fighter
fighter.description: A trained killer: soldier, mercenary, bodyguard or duellist. Fighters wear the best armour they can afford and know how to use every weapon in the rack.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.text: A trained way of fighting, chosen at creation: a Fighting Style feat.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text: The tricks of three kinds of weapon, four from level 4 and five from level 10: a mace that knocks a man down, a rapier that leaves an opening. Change them after a long rest.

features.name: Second Wind
features.text: Once per rest, catch your breath in battle: regain 1d10 + level hit points.

features.name: Action Surge
features.text: Once per rest, push past exhaustion and take a second action on your turn.

features.name: Martial Archetype
features.text: Choose how you fight: Champion or Knight.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: Attack twice when you take the Attack action.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: Fighters train harder than anyone: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.text: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.name: Indomitable
features.text: Once per long rest, reroll a failed saving throw.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: A gift of legend: an epic boon (or another feat), each raising one ability as high as 30.

features.name: Improved Critical
features.text: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.text: Add half your proficiency bonus to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution checks you are not proficient in.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.text: Learn a second fighting style.

knight.name: Knight
knight.text: A shield for others: you hold the line and draw the enemy's blows.

features.name: Hold the Line
features.text: An enemy beside you has disadvantage attacking anyone but you.

features.name: Commanding Presence
features.text: Add your Wisdom bonus to Persuasion and Intimidation when giving orders or demanding surrender.

features.name: Rallying Cry
features.text: When you use Second Wind, friends within 30 feet regain hit points equal to your level.

rogue.name: Rogue
rogue.description: Thief, spy, scout or cutthroat. Rogues live by quick hands, sharp eyes and the knife in the dark, and they rarely fight fair.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Double your proficiency bonus with two chosen skills.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.text: Once per turn, deal extra damage (1d6, growing every other level) when you have advantage, or an ally is fighting your target.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text: The tricks of two kinds of weapon (a rapier that leaves an opening, a dagger quick enough for a second stab). Change them after a long rest.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.text: The secret slang and signs of the criminal world.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.text: Dash, Disengage or Hide with a bonus action, and still attack in the same turn.

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.text: Choose your trade: Thief or Cutthroat.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.text: Once per round, halve the damage of an attack you can see.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Two more skills gain double proficiency.

features.name: Evasion
features.text: Take no damage from area effects you save against, and half if you fail.

cutthroat.name: Cutthroat
cutthroat.text: Killer for hire: the first blow is the last.

features.name: Assassinate
features.text: Advantage against anyone who has not acted yet in a fight; hits on surprised foes are critical.

features.name: Poisoner
features.text: Proficiency with the poisoner's kit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.text: You can maintain a false identity for weeks.

cleric.name: Cleric
cleric.description: A priest with a god's power in their hands. Temples hold divine magic jealously; a cleric heals, blesses and condemns in the name of a faith, and answers to its hierarchy.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text: Pray each morning for the prayers your god will grant today.

features.name: Divine Domain
features.text: Your god's aspect: Life or War.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.text: Once per rest, call on your god directly: Turn Undead, or your domain's power.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.name: Destroy Undead
features.text: Weak undead that you turn are destroyed outright.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: +2 to one ability, or +1 to two.

features.name: Divine Intervention
features.text: Beg your god to act. It rarely listens.

life.name: Life Domain
life.text: Healers and midwives of the faith.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.text: Your healing spells restore 2 + the spell's level extra hit points.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.text: Share out healing equal to five times your level among the wounded.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.text: Healing others heals you a little too.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.text: Once per turn your weapon deals an extra 1d8 radiant damage.

war.name: War Domain
war.text: Chaplains of armies and the gods of battle.

features.name: War Priest
features.text: A few times per rest, make an extra weapon attack.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
features.text: Add +10 to one attack roll.

features.name: War God's Blessing
features.text: Grant an ally +10 on an attack.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.text: Once per turn your weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage.

wizard.name: Wizard
wizard.description: A scholar of forbidden power. Wizards learn magic from books, at ruinous cost in years and coin; some kingdoms license them, others burn them.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text: Cast spells from your spellbook; copy new ones from scrolls and books.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.text: Once a day, after a short rest, recover spent spell slots (total levels up to half your level).

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.text: Choose your school: Evocation or Abjuration.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
